buildRationale: The repository documents two build scripts. `build` is `nx affected --target=build`, which computes what changed relative to a base and therefore builds NOTHING on a freshly cloned, unmodified tree - leaving the workspace package outputs its tests import missing. `build:all` is `nx run-many --target=build`, the repository own script for building every package unconditionally, which is what a clean environment needs. Choosing between two of the repository documented scripts, with the reason recorded; not a bespoke command invented for this harness.

testCommandRationale: nx is the orchestrator TanStack tests through, so it is invoked directly rather than approximated with a hand-built vitest exclusion list. run-many rather than affected: nx.json sets defaultBase main and CI supplies NX_BASE/NX_HEAD from a PR diff via nrwl/nx-set-shas, so on an unmodified clone at main affected computes zero projects and runs nothing. run-many is TanStack own non-PR CI form (test = test:ci = nx run-many). Same relationship as build:all to build.

testCommandRationale: The root package.json has NO scripts block at all - CI drives tests through mise tasks - so there is no root script to select. The root ships its own vitest.config.ts declaring projects: [pkgs/*], and bare `vitest run` against it is the repository own declaration of its test surface. This is the identical uniform non-interactive invocation applied to hono. No project filter, exclusion, or include glob was invented: each package own committed config decides its file set. Narrowing to pkgs/core alone was considered and REJECTED - it would pre-screen the repository into a friendlier shape, which is a form of tuning. Checked in advance because the validation contract forbids launching a browser: pkgs/core/vitest.config.ts imports @vitest/browser-playwright but leaves the browser instance commented out (enabled only by the separate test/browser task via --browser), so `vitest run` runs in node.
buildRationale: No build. pkgs/core exports map points at ./src/index.ts, so workspace consumers (tz, utc, docs) resolve TypeScript source and vitest transpiles it - the same situation as vue, where a build would have been required only if tests imported package outputs.
lockfile: pnpm-lock.yaml committed. Unlike hono and fastify, this repository pins its dependency tree, so two installs a week apart resolve the same versions. No packageManager field, so corepack uses its default pnpm.
